c01s03.title: Two people, several differences
c01s03.caption: The case varies age and experience together; it cannot isolate development.

c01s03b.title: Ask which change is measured
c01s03b.caption: Neither design automatically isolates every developmental cause.

c01s04.title: A fairer comparison
c01s04.caption: An accessible procedure can change measured performance.

c01s05.title: Interpret an age comparison
c01s05.caption: Age differences need a design that examines alternative explanations.

c02s03.title: An exposure needs detail
c02s03.caption: A general risk claim cannot determine an individual pregnancy outcome.

c02s03b.title: Increased risk is not certainty
c02s03b.caption: Risk describes probability under conditions, not a verdict about one family.

c02s04.title: From concern to an appropriate action
c02s04.caption: Developmental science informs support; it does not license retrospective blame.

c02s05.title: Read a prenatal-risk claim
c02s05.caption: Ethical observational research supports bounded risk estimates.

c03s03.title: From response to inference
c03s03.caption: A measured response supports an inference with alternatives.

c03s03b.title: Two routes to evidence
c03s03b.caption: Task differences can change performance without resolving all conceptual questions.

c03s04.title: Keep the observation specific
c03s04.caption: Use developmental findings without assessing a child from a single episode.

c03s05.title: Observation and explanation
c03s05.caption: An infant’s response is evidence, not a complete reading of the mind.

c04s03.title: A rule meets a new example
c04s03.caption: This illustrates conceptual revision, not a fixed age schedule.

c04s03b.title: Support, then check independence
c04s03b.caption: Supported success and independent application answer different questions.

c04s04.title: A fair language question
c04s04.caption: A single conversation does not measure a child’s total language ability.

c04s05.title: Evaluate a teaching claim
c04s05.caption: Name the conditions under which a learner succeeds.

c05s03.title: Safety and exploration interact
c05s03.caption: The sequence is illustrative, not an assessment of attachment security.

c05s03b.title: Different questions
c05s03b.caption: The constructs overlap in influences but are not interchangeable.

c05s04.title: A proportionate interpretation
c05s04.caption: Developmental associations do not determine one person’s future.

c05s05.title: Association is not destiny
c05s05.caption: Early relationships matter without fixing an individual future.

c06s03.title: Map the settings
c06s03.caption: Different contexts supply different opportunities to participate.

c06s03b.title: A correlation needs alternatives
c06s03b.caption: Shared conditions can also affect both sides of a relationship.

c06s04.title: Find a modifiable condition
c06s04.caption: Support should respond to the actual setting rather than a stereotype.

c06s05.title: Keep an ecological explanation testable
c06s05.caption: A contextual map generates questions rather than proving causes.

c07s03.title: Same person, different context
c07s03.caption: Context may contribute to the difference and can be investigated.

c07s03b.title: Support a safer decision
c07s03b.caption: Age-sensitive support can preserve meaningful participation.

c07s04.title: Read an adolescent claim carefully
c07s04.caption: No single age threshold captures every aspect of development.

c07s05.title: Development and agency
c07s05.caption: Developmental trends can guide support without reducing a person to age.

c08s03.title: Timing needs a reference
c08s03.caption: A cultural timetable does not define universal psychological success.

c08s03b.title: Understand a transition
c08s03b.caption: A transition is understood through demands, resources and relationships.

c08s04.title: Several routes to adaptation
c08s04.caption: Adaptation can involve changing priorities as well as improving performance.

c08s05.title: Judge a transition in context
c08s05.caption: A life-course description is not a moral ranking of life paths.

c09s03.title: Different demands
c09s03.caption: Task-specific changes need not move together.

c09s03b.title: Respond proportionately
c09s03b.caption: Accessibility and appropriate care address different needs.

c09s04.title: Avoid a diagnosis from a stereotype
c09s04.caption: Neither age nor one error establishes dementia.

c09s05.title: Three different questions
c09s05.caption: Population ageing findings are not diagnostic rules.

c10s03.title: Build an account
c10s03.caption: A developmental account specifies a pathway rather than a fixed identity.

c10s03b.title: Test a practical support
c10s03b.caption: A benefit must be measured against the goal and its limits.

c10s04.title: A responsible recommendation
c10s04.caption: Use developmental science to improve questions and opportunities.

c10s05.title: From explanation to a fair action
c10s05.caption: A useful explanation supports proportionate, revisable action.
